To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the rostral brain regions, such as the preoptic area and the nucleus of the solitary tract, respond directly to endotoxin or interleukin 1 with the consequetn development of fever and the accompanying acute phase responses.

the rostral regions of the hypothalamus, such as nucleus of the brachium of the stria terminalis, preoptic and anterior regions, responded directly to the injection of either endogenous pyrogen, or interleukin 1, with the consequent generation of fever and acute-phase responses.
fever and the acute phase responses are produced by microinjection of pyrogen into the rostral brain regions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the brain regions that mediate the development of acute‐phase responses accompanying fever in response to endogenous pyrogens.
the brain areas which mediate the development of the fever and the acute phase responses.
the effects of microinjections of rabbit endogenous (pyrogen and recombinant human interleukin‐α) in forty different brain areas on fever and acute phase reactions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the rostral brain regions, including the preoptic area, anterior hypothalamic area and nucleus broca ventrals, are involved in the development and expression of the acute phase responses accompanying the fever.
the rostral regions of the hypothalamus are the primary sites where fever and acute phase reactions are induced by endogenous pyrogen.
the rostral part of the anterior hypothalamic nucleus and nucleus broca ventrals are the major sites of the fever and acute phase response induced by endogenous pyrogen in rabbits.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
endogenous pyrogen, which is produced by peripheral macrophages, acts on the rostral hypothalamus to produce fever and acute phase reactions.
endogenous pyrogen, interleukin‐ 1, iron and zinc are involved in the pathogenesis of fever and acute‐phase responses.
endogenous pyrogen/interleukin‐1‐induced fever and acute phase response are produced by the activation of the hypothalamic regions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can now measure the effects of a drug on the brain in a way that is more sensitive and more specific than ever before.
fever is not the only response to endogenous pyrogens.
the rostral brain regions are important for the regulation of fever and acute‐phase responses.
